items.label: Gist 2.3 port against Gist's own sample run
items.detail_template: Gist's printed weights through our kernel give its printed training discriminants within {kd:.3f} (weight rounding). Retrained with the sample's settings and seed: objective {obj:.7f} against Gist's 0.0173686, {w} of {n} weights equal as printed, {it} passes against 200. The sample came from Gist 2.0.

cause.summary: A worked example of the feature vector (AGLP to KFFK, dMAX = 2); nothing to recompute.
Pseudocode of the Distance-based Top-1-gram vector; it is the method, implemented in features.py.

assumptions.sensitivity: The markers sit within 0.1 of these values on the fitted x axis; the paper names only 150

assumptions.what: Normalized kernel values that round above 1 (identical sequences) are capped at 1, where Gist's code sets them to 0 off the diagonal
assumptions.sensitivity: With Gist's 0 the dMAX = 0 training diverges to NaN (Gist would loop forever); at dMAX = 150 the SVM-DR weights of family 2.5.1.3 become 1.3 times the published ones (Fig. 4B Spearman 0.963 against 0.9999, Fig. 5C r 0.85 against 0.9999; output/causes/weight_scale_dr.json)

assumptions.what: Gist seeds its random update order from the clock; we use seed 1
assumptions.sensitivity: Seeds 2 and 3 move the 2.5.1.3 weights' L2 maximum by under 0.5% (output/causes/weight_scale_dr.json)

assumptions.what: Top-1-gram profiles built as in the paper's ref. [28] (Liu et al. 2008): PSI-BLAST (BLAST+ 2.17.0) with default settings and 10 iterations against the lab's 2016 nrdb90 (Pse-in-One 2.0); last-round hits with E <= 0.002, rows under 98% identity, Henikoff weights, BLOSUM62 pseudocounts with beta = 10; Top-1-gram = largest target frequency (profile2008.py)
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper names only 'a non-redundant database' and cites ref. [28] for the profiles. cause.summary: The SVM-DT curve rises and flattens as published but sits 0.008 to 0.021 ROC above the published points (0.957 against 0.948 at dMAX 150). Our profiles follow the paper's ref. [28] but come from the lab's 2016 nrdb90, while the paper names only 'a non-redundant database' and its copy is not available. The 3-iteration profiles gave 0.950 at dMAX 150 (output/causes/dt_profiles_2008.json).

hypotheses.hypothesis: The difference enters with the profiles: everything after the Top-1-gram sequences is shared with SVM-DR
hypotheses.test: The same features, Gist port and weight code on residues reproduce Fig. 4B (Spearman 0.9999) and Fig. 5C-D (bar values r >= 0.9997)

hypotheses.test: Rerun at dMAX 150 with that rule on the earlier 3-iteration profiles (output/causes/dt_variants.json)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Top-1-gram from the log-odds scores instead of the observed percentages
hypotheses.test: Rerun at dMAX 150 on the earlier 3-iteration profiles (output/causes/dt_variants.json)

cause.summary: ROC comes back exactly (0.919); ROC50 does not with the stated definition (0.497 against 0.715). Our ROC matches at every dMAX, so the rankings agree and the gap is in how ROC50 was computed. The paper's values match an ordinary ROC on the ranking cut at the 50th false positive, which divides by the positives found there instead of by all positives (0.712 against 0.715).

hypotheses.hypothesis: ROC50 as Gribskov and Robinson's normalized area to the first 50 false positives (the stated definition)
hypotheses.test: roc.py on our discriminants at dMAX 150: SVM-DR 0.497, SVM-DT 0.720 (tables.json)

hypotheses.hypothesis: ROC50 as the true-positive rate at the 50th false positive
hypotheses.test: SVM-DR 0.662, SVM-DT 0.814 at dMAX 150 (output/causes/roc50_variants.json)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Seed of Gist's update order
hypotheses.test: Seed 2: SVM-DR ROC50 0.4973 against 0.4970 (output/causes/dr_variants.json)

hypotheses.hypothesis: The printed values behave like ROC_n with a larger n
hypotheses.test: Searched n: ROC_200 gives SVM-DR 0.720 (paper 0.715); for SVM-DT, whose ROC itself differs, 0.855 (paper 0.800). Found by search, no mechanism (output/causes/roc50_variants.json)

hypotheses.hypothesis: ROC50 as an ordinary ROC computed on the ranking cut at the 50th false positive: the area to 50 false positives divided by the true positives found there instead of by all positives (positives ranked below the cut drop out)
hypotheses.test: SVM-DR 0.712 (paper 0.715) at dMAX 150, no free parameter; SVM-DT 0.838 (paper 0.800), above the paper as its ROC is (0.957 against 0.948); with the earlier 3-iteration profiles, whose ROC was closer (0.950), 0.790 (output/causes/roc50_variants.json, roc_on_cut_list). It also brings back the paper's ROC50 comparisons: SVM-DR above Monomer-dist (0.712 against 0.508) and SVM-DT above SVM-Top-n-gram (14.2 points; paper 10.4). It is what an ordinary ROC routine, such as Gist's gist-score-svm, gives on a ranking cut at 50 false positives. The paper gives no ROC50 code or per-family values to confirm it, and SVM-DT runs on other profiles

hypotheses.hypothesis: ROC50 as the area to a false positive rate of 0.5 (or 0.1), divided by that rate
hypotheses.test: FPR 0.5: SVM-DR 0.853, SVM-DT 0.925; FPR 0.1: 0.632 and 0.802 at dMAX 150 (output/causes/roc50_variants.json)

hypotheses.hypothesis: ROC50 as the area to a false positive rate of 0.5 (or 0.1), divided by that rate
hypotheses.test: FPR 0.5: SVM-DR 0.853, SVM-DT 0.925; FPR 0.1: 0.632 and 0.802 at dMAX 150 (output/causes/roc50_variants.json)

[28] (Liu et al. 2008): PSI-BLAST (BLAST+ 2.17.0) with default settings and 10 iterations against the lab's 2016 nrdb90 (Pse-in-One 2.0); last-round hits with E <= 0.002, rows under 98% identity, Henikoff weights, BLOSUM62 pseudocounts with beta = 10; Top-1-gram = largest target frequency (profile2008.py)
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper names only 'a non-redundant database' and cites ref. [28] for the profiles. With the lab's 2017 settings instead (3 iterations, E = 0.001, largest observed percentage; top1.py) the mean ROC at dMAX 150 is 0.9502 instead of 0.9570 and family 2.5.1.3's ROC 0.961 instead of 0.993 (output/causes/dt_profiles_2008.json)

cause.summary: Our SVM-DT reaches ROC 0.957, above every quoted profile method including SVM-PDT-Profile (0.950), where the paper's 0.948 is below it. Our SVM-DT sits about 0.01 above the paper at every dMAX (profiles from the 2016 nrdb90), enough to change this ranking. With the 3-iteration profiles it was 0.9502, above SVM-PDT-Profile by 0.0002.
